Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning obeying officers and signs, driving on the right and when the left half may be used, passing on the right, lane use, following distance, divided highways, required signals, railroad crossings, speed rules, prohibited parking, tow-away zones, unattended vehicles, emergency vehicles, funeral processions, the slow-moving vehicle emblem, no-passing situations and right-of-way rules in plain English.

Prerequisites: basic road vocabulary such as lane, intersection, crosswalk and shoulder; this chapter is the legal core the later technique chapters build on.

Scope note: obeying officers and traffic control devices, driving on the right and the exceptions for using the left half, passing on the right, lane use, following distance, divided highways, required signals, railroad crossing stops, speed laws and reduced-speed areas, prohibited parking places, tow-away zones, interference with the driver, unattended vehicles, emergency vehicles, funeral processions, the slow-moving vehicle emblem, the six no-passing situations and the basic right-of-way rules. Signs, signals and markings follow in the next three sections.

Recall emphasis: the distances and parking limits are practiced as recall items, while right-of-way and no-passing decisions feed the dedicated scene-decision surface declared in part C.
